_about: Design and check rules per manufacturing process. Used by tools/partcheck.py and tools/make_viewer.py; mirrored for the CAD side in lib/process.scad (keep the two in step). Wall limits follow what the services' own checks reject (red) and flag (warn). Rates are rough per-cm3 figures from real JLC quotes; always upload the file for a real price. short, for and look are the plain-words name, the one-line purpose and the material look the preview page uses. Home printers (home: true, fdm_pla and fdm_petg) are checked against a build volume (default 220 x 220 x 250 mm; printer.json in the project, --bed or BED=256x256x256 override it) and report filament instead of a service price. Home-printer sources, read 2026-11-18: Prusa Knowledge Base, PLA (help.prusa3d.com/article/pla_2062: 215/210 C nozzle, 60 C bed, softens above 60 C, not for outdoor use) and PETG (help.prusa3d.com/article/petg_2059: 230-240 C nozzle, 85-90 C bed, exterior use under 80 C, prone to stringing, do not print on the smooth PEI sheet: adhesion may be too strong); the same page says other makers' PLA runs 185-235 C. Densities 1.24 (PLA) and 1.27 (PETG) g/cm3 are the usual datasheet values (Prusament). Filament rate = about 20 USD/kg x density, a typical spool price. Temperature ranges here are the typical spread across makers; the spool label wins.

resin_sla.name: Resin (SLA), prototype
resin_sla.for: A cheap, quick test print to check fit and feel before the real thing. Brittle, and not for life outdoors.
notes: The service adds and removes supports itself; overhangs are not your problem, trapped resin is.
A closed cavity holds liquid resin. Every hollow needs a drain hole of at least 2 mm.
Brittle and UV-sensitive. Tests fit, feel and function, not life outdoors. Hand-tight only.

fdm_asa.name: FDM, ASA plastic, final part
fdm_asa.for: A tough plastic that lasts outdoors in sun and water. The usual choice for a finished plastic part.
notes: Walls: under one 0.4 mm line cannot print; under two lines (0.8) prints weak.
Print with the largest flat face on the bed; chamfer the bed edge 0.6-1 mm against elephant foot.
Flat ceilings bridge fine up to about 10 mm; past that, slope them 45 degrees.
Horizontal holes over 6 mm: teardrop them (hole_x in process.scad).
Layer lines are the weak direction: load across them, not along them.
Rate is filament only, at 100 % fill (upper bound).

fdm_pla.name: Home printer, PLA
fdm_pla.for: The easy filament for test fits and indoor parts on your own printer. Softens in the heat, so not for outdoors.
notes: Walls: under one 0.4 mm line cannot print; under two lines (0.8) prints weak; 1.2 mm is better for strength.
PLA softens at about 55-60 C: not for a car, hot sun or hot water. Use it for indoor parts and test fits.
Print with the largest flat face on the bed; chamfer the bed edge 0.6-1 mm against elephant foot.
Layer lines are the weak direction: load across them, not along them.
Print threads coarse (M8 and up), or use a heat-set insert or a nut trap instead of a fine thread.
Rate is filament only (about 20 USD/kg, 1.24 g/cm3) at 100 % fill, an upper bound.

fdm_petg.name: Home printer, PETG
fdm_petg.for: A tougher home-printer filament that takes heat up to about 70-80 C. Fine for most outdoor parts.
notes: Walls: under one 0.4 mm line cannot print; under two lines (0.8) prints weak; 1.2 mm is better for strength.
Takes about 70-80 C, is tougher than PLA and fine for most outdoor parts (it yellows slowly in sun; ASA is better for years outdoors).
PETG strings (cooling and retraction help) and sticks very hard to a smooth PEI bed: use a textured sheet or a glue stick.
Layer lines are the weak direction: load across them, not along them.
Print threads coarse (M8 and up), or use a heat-set insert or a nut trap instead of a fine thread.
Rate is filament only (about 20 USD/kg, 1.27 g/cm3) at 100 % fill, an upper bound.

slm_316l.name: Metal (SLM), 316L stainless
slm_316l.for: Printed metal for parts that must be strong, take heat or last for decades. Priced by how much metal is in it.
notes: No flat ceilings: every downward face steeper than 45 degrees, or a support nobody can reach inside.
Powder must pour out: no closed cavities.
Threads print rough on the downward flanks: print loose (0.45) and chase with a tap.
Food-equipment alloy; no galling against brass; fine outdoors. Not a certified drinking-water fitting.
Rate: JLC quote, 38 cm3 part at $67.

slm_alsi10mg.name: Metal (SLM), aluminium AlSi10Mg
slm_alsi10mg.for: Printed metal at about half the weight and price of steel. Needs care against corrosion next to brass or steel in water.
notes: Same geometry rules as 316L.
Against brass, nickel or steel in water it corrodes slowly: PTFE tape on threads, anodize if offered, dry it over winter.
Rate: JLC quote, 38 cm3 part at $41.

mjf_pa12.name: Nylon (MJF/SLS), PA12
mjf_pa12.for: A tough, slightly flexible plastic printed in powder, so any shape prints without supports.
notes: Self-supporting in its powder bed: any overhang prints.
Powder must escape: hollows need two openings of 4 mm or more.
Tougher than resin and fine outdoors; slightly porous, so seal with a gasket, not the surface.
